1.name: Al-Baqarah
1.overview: It is the second chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran and the longest one, consisting of 286 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the story of the cow mentioned in it. It addresses a wide range of themes, including the Oneness of God, guidance, the Children of Israel, the People of the Book, laws and legislation, charity, fasting, pilgrimage, and matters of faith and morality. It also contains Ayat al-Kursi (the Verse of the Throne).

1.name: Aal Imran
1.overview: Surah Aal-Imran teaches that true faith requires conviction, obedience, unity, patience, and steadfastness. Through the stories of earlier prophets and the lessons of Uhud, it encourages believers to remain faithful to Allah and His guidance even when facing trials.

1.name: An-Nisa
1.overview: It is the fourth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 176 verses. It is a Medinan surah that addresses many issues related to women, family, inheritance, and marriage. It also discusses the rights of orphans, the People of the Book, and matters of justice and community life.

1.name: Al-Ma'idah
1.overview: It is the fifth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 120 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the table (ma'idah) mentioned in the story of Jesus and his disciples. It addresses themes such as the fulfillment of covenants, lawful and unlawful food, justice, the People of the Book, and the finality of the message of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

1.name: Al-An'am
1.overview: It is the sixth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 165 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the cattle (an'am) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the refutation of polytheism, the signs of God in creation, the stories of previous prophets, and matters of faith, guidance, and accountability.

1.name: Al-A'raf
1.overview: It is the seventh chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 206 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the heights (al-a'raf) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the stories of the prophets—including Adam, Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, Shu'ayb, and Moses—the consequences of denying God's messengers, the signs of God in creation, and the final accountability of humanity.

1.name: Al-Anfal
1.overview: It is the eighth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 75 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the spoils of war (al-anfal) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the Battle of Badr, the distribution of spoils, the qualities of true believers, obedience to God and His Messenger ﷺ, and matters of war, peace, and treaty obligations.

1.name: At-Tawbah
1.overview: It is the ninth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 129 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from repentance (at-tawbah) mentioned in it. It is the only surah that does not begin with the Basmalah. It addresses themes such as the dissolution of treaties with polytheists, the Battle of Tabuk, the qualities of hypocrites, repentance, charity, and matters of faith, jihad, and the unity of the Muslim community.

1.name: Yunus
1.overview: It is the tenth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 109 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the Prophet Yunus (Jonah) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the truth of revelation, the stories of previous prophets—including Noah, Moses, and Yunus—the fate of those who deny God's signs, and the invitation to reflect on God's mercy and wisdom.

1.name: Hud
1.overview: It is the eleventh chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 123 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the Prophet Hud mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the stories of previous prophets—including Noah, Hud, Salih, Abraham, Lot, Shu'ayb, and Moses—the consequences of denying God's messengers, and the importance of steadfastness and reliance on God.

1.name: Yusuf
1.overview: It is the twelfth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 111 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) mentioned in it. It relates the complete story of Prophet Yusuf—from his childhood dream, being thrown into the well, sold into slavery in Egypt, falsely accused, imprisoned, and eventually rising to a position of authority—highlighting themes of patience, trust in God, forgiveness, and divine wisdom. It is often described as "the best of stories."

1.name: Ar-Ra'd
1.overview: It is the thirteenth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 43 verses. It is a surah that takes its name from thunder (ar-ra'd) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the signs of God in creation, the truth of revelation, the difference between believers and disbelievers, and the inevitability of God's judgment.

1.name: Ibrahim
1.overview: It is the fourteenth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 52 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the truth of revelation, the mission of the prophets, gratitude for God's blessings, and the prayer of Prophet Ibrahim for his descendants and the city of Makkah.

1.name: Al-Hijr
1.overview: It is the fifteenth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 99 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the rocky tract (al-hijr) mentioned in it, associated with the people of Thamud. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the truth of revelation, the stories of previous prophets—including Salih, Abraham, and Lot—the protection of the Quran, and the consequences of denying God's messengers.

1.name: An-Nahl
1.overview: It is the sixteenth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 128 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the bees (an-nahl) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the signs of God in creation, gratitude for God's blessings, the truth of revelation, the refutation of polytheism, and matters of justice, charity, and wisdom.

1.name: Al-Isra
1.overview: It is the seventeenth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 111 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the night journey (al-isra) of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the Night Journey to Jerusalem, the Children of Israel, the Oneness of God, the honor of the Quran, moral and ethical teachings, and the accountability of humanity.

1.name: Al-Kahf
1.overview: It is the eighteenth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 110 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the cave (al-kahf) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the story of the People of the Cave, the story of the rich man and the poor man, the story of Moses and Al-Khidr, and the story of Dhul-Qarnayn. It also highlights themes of faith, patience, humility, the fleeting nature of worldly life, and the signs of God.

1.name: Maryam
1.overview: It is the nineteenth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 98 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from Maryam (Mary), the mother of Prophet Isa (Jesus), mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the story of Zakariyya and Yahya, the miraculous birth of Isa, the stories of Ibrahim and other prophets, the Oneness of God, and the mercy and power of God.

1.name: Ta-Ha
1.overview: It is the twentieth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 135 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the two letters (Ta-Ha) with which it begins. It addresses themes such as the story of Moses—his call by God, his confrontation with Pharaoh, the crossing of the sea, and the incident of the golden calf—as well as the story of Adam, the truth of revelation, and the Oneness of God.

1.name: Al-Anbiya
1.overview: It is the twenty-first chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 112 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the prophets (al-anbiya) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the truth of revelation, the stories of numerous prophets—including Abraham, Lot, Noah, David, Solomon, Job, Zechariah, and Jesus—the signs of God in creation, and the inevitability of accountability and judgment.

1.name: Al-Hajj
1.overview: It is the twenty-second chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 78 verses. It is a surah that takes its name from the pilgrimage (al-hajj) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the signs of God in creation, the Day of Judgment, the sanctity of the Sacred House, the rites of pilgrimage, and matters of faith, sacrifice, and steadfastness.

1.name: Al-Mu'minun
1.overview: It is the twenty-third chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 118 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the believers (al-mu'minun) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the qualities of true believers, the stages of human creation, the signs of God in creation, the stories of previous prophets—including Noah, Moses, and Jesus—and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment.

1.name: An-Nur
1.overview: It is the twenty-fourth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 64 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the light (an-nur) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the light of God, chastity and modesty, the laws concerning adultery and false accusation, the etiquette of entering homes, and matters of faith, morality, and community life.

1.name: Al-Furqan
1.overview: It is the twenty-fifth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 77 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the criterion (al-furqan) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the truth of revelation, the refutation of polytheism, the stories of previous prophets—including Moses and Noah—and the qualities of the true servants of God.

1.name: Ash-Shu'ara
1.overview: It is the twenty-sixth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 227 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the poets (ash-shu'ara) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the truth of revelation, the stories of previous prophets—including Moses, Abraham, Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, and Shu'ayb—the consequences of denying God's messengers, and the distinction between the Quran and poetry.

1.name: An-Naml
1.overview: It is the twenty-seventh chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 93 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the ants (an-naml) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the truth of revelation, the stories of previous prophets—including Moses, David, Solomon, Salih, and Lot—the story of the Queen of Sheba, and the signs of God in creation.

1.name: Al-Qasas
1.overview: It is the twenty-eighth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 88 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the stories (al-qasas) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the story of Moses—from his birth and being placed in the river, to his upbringing in Pharaoh's palace, his escape to Madyan, and his return and confrontation with Pharaoh—as well as the story of Qarun, the Oneness of God, and the promise of victory for the believers.

1.name: Al-Ankabut
1.overview: It is the twenty-ninth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 69 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the spider (al-ankabut) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the reality of trials and tests of faith, the stories of previous prophets—including Noah, Abraham, Lot, Shu'ayb, Moses, and others—the Oneness of God, the truth of revelation, and the fragility of those who rely on other than God.

1.name: Ar-Rum
1.overview: It is the thirtieth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 60 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the Romans (ar-rum) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the prophecy of the Romans' victory, the signs of God in creation, the truth of revelation, the Oneness of God, and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment.

1.name: Luqman
1.overview: It is the thirty-first chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 34 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from Luqman the Wise mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the signs of God in creation, the advice of Luqman to his son—covering wisdom, gratitude, prayer, patience, and humility—and the truth of revelation and accountability.

1.name: As-Sajdah
1.overview: It is the thirty-second chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 30 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the prostration (as-sajdah) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the truth of revelation, the signs of God in creation, the resurrection and accountability, and the qualities of the believers who prostrate themselves before God.

1.name: Al-Ahzab
1.overview: It is the thirty-third chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 73 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the confederates (al-ahzab) mentioned in it, referring to the allied tribes that besieged Madinah in the Battle of the Trench. It addresses themes such as the Battle of the Trench, the status of the Prophet ﷺ, the wives of the Prophet, adoption, the hypocrites, and matters of faith, modesty, and community life.

1.name: Saba
1.overview: It is the thirty-fourth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 54 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the people of Saba (Sheba) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the truth of revelation, the story of David and Solomon, the people of Saba and their ingratitude, the refutation of polytheism, and the inevitability of accountability and judgment.

1.name: Fatir
1.overview: It is the thirty-fifth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 45 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the Originator (Fatir) mentioned at its beginning, one of the names of God. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the signs of God in creation, the truth of revelation, the refutation of polytheism, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Ya-Sin
1.overview: It is the thirty-sixth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 83 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the two letters (Ya-Sin) with which it begins. It addresses themes such as the truth of revelation, the mission of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, the story of the people of the town and the messengers sent to them, the signs of God in creation, the resurrection and accountability, and the power and mercy of God.

1.name: As-Saffat
1.overview: It is the thirty-seventh chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 182 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the ranks (as-saffat) mentioned at its beginning, referring to the angels arranged in rows. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the refutation of polytheism, the stories of previous prophets—including Noah, Abraham, Moses, Aaron, Elias, Lot, Jonah, and the test of Abraham with his son—and the resurrection and accountability.

1.name: Sad
1.overview: It is the thirty-eighth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 88 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the letter (Sad) with which it begins. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the truth of revelation, the stories of previous prophets—including David, Solomon, Job, and Abraham—the consequences of denying God's messengers, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Az-Zumar
1.overview: It is the thirty-ninth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 75 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the crowds (az-zumar) mentioned in it, referring to the groups of people led to Paradise and to Hellfire. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, sincere worship, the mercy of God, repentance, the contrast between believers and disbelievers, and the resurrection and accountability.

1.name: Ghafir
1.overview: It is the fortieth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 85 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the Forgiver (Ghafir) mentioned at its beginning, one of the names of God. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the truth of revelation, the story of Moses and Pharaoh, the believer from Pharaoh's family, the refutation of polytheism, and the inevitability of accountability and judgment.

1.name: Fussilat
1.overview: It is the forty-first chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 54 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the word "fussilat" (explained in detail) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the truth of revelation, the Oneness of God, the signs of God in creation, the story of the people of 'Ad and Thamud, the refutation of polytheism, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Ash-Shura
1.overview: It is the forty-second chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 53 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the consultation (ash-shura) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the truth of revelation, the unity of the message of the prophets, the importance of consultation and justice, forgiveness, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Az-Zukhruf
1.overview: It is the forty-third chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 89 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the ornaments (az-zukhruf) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the truth of revelation, the refutation of polytheism, the stories of previous prophets—including Moses and Abraham—and the fleeting nature of worldly adornments compared to the Hereafter.

1.name: Ad-Dukhan
1.overview: It is the forty-fourth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 59 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the smoke (ad-dukhan) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the truth of revelation, the blessed night in which the Quran was revealed, the story of Moses and Pharaoh, the consequences of denying God's messengers, and the resurrection and accountability.

1.name: Al-Jathiyah
1.overview: It is the forty-fifth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 37 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the kneeling (al-jathiyah) mentioned in it, referring to the nations kneeling on the Day of Judgment. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the signs of God in creation, the truth of revelation, the refutation of polytheism, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Ahqaf
1.overview: It is the forty-sixth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 35 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the sand dunes (al-ahqaf) mentioned in it, referring to the dwelling place of the people of 'Ad. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the truth of revelation, the stories of previous prophets—including Hud and the people of 'Ad—the duty of kindness to parents, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Muhammad
1.overview: It is the forty-seventh chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 38 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the qualities of the believers, the consequences of disbelief and hypocrisy, the obligation of obedience to God and His Messenger ﷺ, the reality of jihad, and the contrast between the worldly life and the Hereafter.

1.name: Al-Fath
1.overview: It is the forty-eighth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 29 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the victory (al-fath) mentioned in it, referring to the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. It addresses themes such as the clear victory granted to the Prophet ﷺ, the allegiance of the believers, the qualities of the companions, the hypocrites and those with weak faith, and the promise of God's support for the believers.

1.name: Al-Hujurat
1.overview: It is the forty-ninth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 18 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the chambers (al-hujurat) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the etiquette of dealing with the Prophet ﷺ, mutual respect among believers, the prohibition of backbiting and suspicion, the importance of verifying news, the equality of all people before God, and the true meaning of faith and piety.

1.name: Qaf
1.overview: It is the fiftieth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 45 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the letter (Qaf) with which it begins. It addresses themes such as the truth of revelation, the Oneness of God, the signs of God in creation, the resurrection and accountability, and the nearness of God to His servants.

1.name: Azariyat
1.overview: It is the fifty-first chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 60 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the winds that scatter (adh-dhariyat) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the truth of revelation, the Oneness of God, the signs of God in creation, the stories of previous prophets—including Abraham, Lot, and Moses—the resurrection and accountability, and the purpose of creation.

1.name: At-Tur
1.overview: It is the fifty-second chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 49 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the mount (at-tur) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the truth of revelation, the Oneness of God, the reality of the Day of Judgment, the refutation of the disbelievers' claims, the signs of God in creation, and the reward of the righteous.

1.name: An-Najm
1.overview: It is the fifty-third chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 62 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the star (an-najm) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the truth of revelation, the authenticity of the Prophet's ﷺ message, the refutation of polytheism, the signs of God in creation, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Qamar
1.overview: It is the fifty-fourth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 55 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the moon (al-qamar) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the splitting of the moon as a sign, the truth of revelation, the stories of previous prophets—including Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, Lot, and Pharaoh—the consequences of denying God's messengers, and the resurrection and accountability.

1.name: Ar-Rahman
1.overview: It is the fifty-fifth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 78 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman) mentioned at its beginning, one of the names of God. It addresses themes such as the mercy of God, the signs of God in creation, the blessings bestowed upon humanity and jinn, the reality of the Hereafter, and the accountability of humanity before God. It is known for its recurring refrain: "So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?"

1.name: Al-Waqi'ah
1.overview: It is the fifty-sixth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 96 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the event (al-waqi'ah) mentioned at its beginning, referring to the Day of Judgment. It addresses themes such as the reality of the Hereafter, the three categories of people—the foremost, the companions of the right, and the companions of the left—the signs of God in creation, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Hadid
1.overview: It is the fifty-seventh chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 29 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from iron (al-hadid) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, His power and knowledge, the importance of faith and charity, the contrast between the worldly life and the Hereafter, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Mujadilah
1.overview: It is the fifty-eighth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 22 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the woman who disputes (al-mujadilah) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the laws concerning divorce by zihar, the omniscience of God, the etiquette of gatherings, the prohibition of secret consultations for sin, and the qualities of the believers and hypocrites.

1.name: Al-Hashr
1.overview: It is the fifty-ninth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 24 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the gathering (al-hashr) mentioned in it, referring to the expulsion of the Banu Nadir tribe. It addresses themes such as the power of God, the distribution of spoils, the qualities of the believers and hypocrites, the importance of reflecting on the Quran, and the names and attributes of God.

1.name: Al-Mumtahanah
1.overview: It is the sixtieth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 13 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the woman who is tested (al-mumtahanah) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the prohibition of alliance with those who fight the believers, the importance of faith and loyalty to God, the treatment of believing women who emigrate, and the qualities of true believers.

1.name: As-Saff
1.overview: It is the sixty-first chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 14 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the ranks (as-saff) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the importance of unity and sincerity in striving for God's cause, the call to support God's religion, the mission of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and the example of the disciples of Jesus.

1.name: Al-Jumu'ah
1.overview: It is the sixty-second chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 11 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from Friday (al-jumu'ah) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the mission of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, the failure of the People of the Book to act upon their knowledge, the importance of the Friday prayer, and the contrast between those who prioritize worldly gain and those who seek God's reward.

1.name: Al-Munafiqun
1.overview: It is the sixty-third chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 11 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the hypocrites (al-munafiqun) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the characteristics of the hypocrites, their deception and false oaths, the importance of sincerity in faith, the distribution of wealth, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: At-Taghabun
1.overview: It is the sixty-fourth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 18 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the mutual disillusionment (at-taghabun) mentioned in it, referring to the Day of Judgment. It addresses themes such as the Oneness of God, the signs of God in creation, the truth of revelation, the contrast between believers and disbelievers, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: At-Talaq
1.overview: It is the sixty-fifth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 12 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from divorce (at-talaq) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the laws of divorce, the waiting period (iddah), the rights of women and children, the importance of piety and trust in God, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: At-Tahrim
1.overview: It is the sixty-sixth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 12 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the prohibition (at-tahrim) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the importance of maintaining family ties and faith, the examples of believing and disbelieving women—including the wives of Noah and Lot, the wife of Pharaoh, and Maryam—repentance, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Mulk
1.overview: It is the sixty-seventh chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 30 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the dominion (al-mulk) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the sovereignty of God, the signs of God in creation, the truth of revelation, the reality of the Hereafter, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Qalam
1.overview: It is the sixty-eighth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 52 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the pen (al-qalam) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the truth of revelation, the noble character of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, the refutation of the disbelievers' claims, the story of the owners of the garden, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Haqqah
1.overview: It is the sixty-ninth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 52 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the inevitable reality (al-haqqah) mentioned at its beginning, referring to the Day of Judgment. It addresses themes such as the reality of the Hereafter, the stories of previous nations—including 'Ad, Thamud, and Pharaoh—the truth of revelation, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Ma'arij
1.overview: It is the seventieth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 44 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the ascending stairways (al-ma'arij) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the reality of the Day of Judgment, the attributes of God, the qualities of the believers—including patience, prayer, charity, and chastity—and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Nuh
1.overview: It is the seventy-first chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 28 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the Prophet Nuh (Noah) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the mission of Prophet Nuh, his call to his people to worship God alone, the consequences of denying God's messengers, and the mercy and justice of God.

1.name: Al-Jinn
1.overview: It is the seventy-second chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 28 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the jinn mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the hearing of the Quran by a group of jinn, their acceptance of faith, the Oneness of God, the refutation of polytheism, the knowledge of the unseen belonging to God alone, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Muzzammil
1.overview: It is the seventy-third chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 20 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the one who is wrapped (al-muzzammil) mentioned at its beginning, referring to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. It addresses themes such as the night prayer, the recitation of the Quran, patience and steadfastness in the face of opposition, the remembrance of God, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Muddaththir
1.overview: It is the seventy-fourth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 56 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the one who is cloaked (al-muddaththir) mentioned at its beginning, referring to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. It addresses themes such as the command to rise and warn, the greatness of God, the purification of the soul, the reality of the Day of Judgment, the story of the disbeliever who rejected the Quran, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Qiyamah
1.overview: It is the seventy-fifth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 40 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the resurrection (al-qiyamah) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the reality of the Day of Judgment, the resurrection of humanity, the accountability of deeds, the denial of the disbelievers, and the power of God over all things.

1.name: Al-Insan
1.overview: It is the seventy-sixth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 31 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from man (al-insan) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the creation of humanity, the guidance of God, the reward of the righteous in Paradise, the importance of charity and feeding the poor, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Mursalat
1.overview: It is the seventy-seventh chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 50 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from those sent forth (al-mursalat) mentioned at its beginning, referring to the winds or angels. It addresses themes such as the truth of revelation, the reality of the Day of Judgment, the signs of God in creation, the consequences of denying God's messengers, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: An-Naba
1.overview: It is the seventy-eighth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 40 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the great news (an-naba) mentioned at its beginning, referring to the Day of Judgment. It addresses themes such as the reality of the Hereafter, the signs of God in creation, the resurrection and accountability, and the contrast between the reward of the righteous and the punishment of the wicked.

1.name: An-Nazi'at
1.overview: It is the seventy-ninth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 46 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from those who pull out (an-nazi'at) mentioned at its beginning, referring to the angels. It addresses themes such as the reality of the Day of Judgment, the story of Moses and Pharaoh, the signs of God in creation, the resurrection and accountability, and the fate of the righteous and the wicked.

1.name: Abasa
1.overview: It is the eightieth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 42 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the word "abasa" (he frowned) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the honor of the blind man, the importance of caring for the needy, the signs of God in creation, the resurrection and accountability, and the contrast between the grateful and the ungrateful.

1.name: At-Takwir
1.overview: It is the eighty-first chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 29 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the folding up (at-takwir) mentioned at its beginning, referring to the folding of the sun on the Day of Judgment. It addresses themes such as the cosmic events of the Day of Judgment, the truth of revelation, the mission of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Infitar
1.overview: It is the eighty-second chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 19 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the splitting (al-infitar) mentioned at its beginning, referring to the splitting of the sky on the Day of Judgment. It addresses themes such as the cosmic events of the Day of Judgment, the accountability of human deeds, the honor of the recording angels, and the reality of the Hereafter.

1.name: Al-Mutaffifin
1.overview: It is the eighty-third chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 36 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the defrauders (al-mutaffifin) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the prohibition of cheating in trade, the reality of the Day of Judgment, the record of deeds, the fate of the righteous and the wicked, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Inshiqaq
1.overview: It is the eighty-fourth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 25 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the splitting (al-inshiqaq) mentioned at its beginning, referring to the splitting of the sky on the Day of Judgment. It addresses themes such as the cosmic events of the Day of Judgment, the accountability of human deeds, the record of deeds, and the fate of the righteous and the wicked.

1.name: Al-Buruj
1.overview: It is the eighty-fifth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 22 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the constellations (al-buruj) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the story of the people of the trench, the persecution of the believers, the power and justice of God, the truth of revelation, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: At-Tariq
1.overview: It is the eighty-sixth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 17 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the night star (at-tariq) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the signs of God in creation, the creation of humanity, the truth of revelation, the reality of the Day of Judgment, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-A'la
1.overview: It is the eighty-seventh chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 19 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the Most High (al-a'la) mentioned at its beginning, one of the names of God. It addresses themes such as the glorification of God, the signs of God in creation, the truth of revelation, the reminder and guidance, and the contrast between the worldly life and the Hereafter.

1.name: Al-Ghashiyah
1.overview: It is the eighty-eighth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 26 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the overwhelming event (al-ghashiyah) mentioned at its beginning, referring to the Day of Judgment. It addresses themes such as the reality of the Hereafter, the signs of God in creation, the mission of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as a reminder, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Fajr
1.overview: It is the eighty-ninth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 30 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the dawn (al-fajr) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the stories of previous nations—including 'Ad, Thamud, and Pharaoh—the reality of the Day of Judgment, the accountability of human deeds, the nature of the human soul, and the reward of the righteous.

1.name: Al-Balad
1.overview: It is the ninetieth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 20 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the city (al-balad) mentioned at its beginning, referring to Makkah. It addresses themes such as the sanctity of Makkah, the struggles of human life, the obligation of charity and compassion, the signs of God in creation, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Ash-Shams
1.overview: It is the ninety-first chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 15 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the sun (ash-shams) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the signs of God in creation, the purification of the soul, the story of the people of Thamud and their rejection of Prophet Salih, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Layl
1.overview: It is the ninety-second chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 21 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the night (al-layl) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the contrast between those who give in charity and those who are stingy, the diversity of human endeavors, the reward of the righteous, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Ad-Duha
1.overview: It is the ninety-third chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 11 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the morning brightness (ad-duha) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the comfort and reassurance given to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, the bounty and mercy of God, the care for orphans and the needy, and the importance of gratitude and remembrance of God's blessings.

1.name: Ash-Sharh
1.overview: It is the ninety-fourth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 8 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the expansion (ash-sharh) mentioned at its beginning, referring to the expansion of the Prophet's ﷺ breast. It addresses themes such as the comfort and ease granted by God after hardship, the importance of patience and trust in God, and the call to strive in worship and devotion.

1.name: At-Tin
1.overview: It is the ninety-fifth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 8 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the fig (at-tin) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the honor of humanity, the signs of God in creation, the truth of revelation, the reality of the Day of Judgment, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Alaq
1.overview: It is the ninety-sixth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 19 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the clot (al-alaq) mentioned in it. It is notable for containing the first verses revealed of the Quran, beginning with the command to "Read." It addresses themes such as the pursuit of knowledge, the creation of humanity, the generosity of God, the transgression of the arrogant, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Qadr
1.overview: It is the ninety-seventh chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 5 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the decree/night of power (al-qadr) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the revelation of the Quran in the Night of Power, the greatness and blessings of this night, the descent of the angels, and the peace that prevails until dawn.

1.name: Al-Bayyinah
1.overview: It is the ninety-eighth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 8 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the clear evidence (al-bayyinah) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the clear proof sent by God, the stance of the People of the Book and the polytheists toward it, the importance of sincere worship, and the reward of the righteous and the fate of the disbelievers.

1.name: Az-Zalzalah
1.overview: It is the ninety-ninth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 8 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the earthquake (az-zalzalah) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the cosmic events of the Day of Judgment, the earth bearing witness to human deeds, the accountability of every soul, and the recompense for even the smallest good or evil deed.

1.name: Al-Adiyat
1.overview: It is the one hundredth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 11 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the charging steeds (al-adiyat) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the ungratefulness of humanity, the love of wealth, the signs of God in creation, and the accountability of humanity before God on the Day of Judgment.

1.name: Al-Qari'ah
1.overview: It is the one hundred and first chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 11 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the striking calamity (al-qari'ah) mentioned at its beginning, referring to the Day of Judgment. It addresses themes such as the terrifying events of the Day of Judgment, the weighing of deeds, and the fate of those whose good deeds outweigh their evil deeds versus those whose deeds are light.

1.name: At-Takathur
1.overview: It is the one hundred and second chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 8 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the rivalry in accumulation (at-takathur) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the distraction of worldly competition, the heedlessness of humanity, the reality of the Hereafter, and the accountability of humanity before God.

1.name: Al-Asr
1.overview: It is the one hundred and third chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 3 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from time (al-asr) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the state of humanity in loss, the importance of faith, good deeds, advising one another to truth, and advising one another to patience.

1.name: Al-Humazah
1.overview: It is the one hundred and fourth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 9 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the slanderer (al-humazah) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the warning against backbiting, slander, and the hoarding of wealth, the punishment of those who mock others, and the reality of the Hereafter.

1.name: Al-Fil
1.overview: It is the one hundred and fifth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 5 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the elephant (al-fil) mentioned in it. It addresses the story of the People of the Elephant who attempted to destroy the Kaaba, and how God destroyed them with flocks of birds pelting them with stones of baked clay, highlighting God's power and protection of His Sacred House.

1.name: Quraysh
1.overview: It is the one hundred and sixth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 4 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the tribe of Quraysh mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the blessings and security granted by God to the Quraysh, their trade caravans in winter and summer, and the call to worship the Lord of the Sacred House alone in gratitude for His favors.

1.name: Al-Ma'un
1.overview: It is the one hundred and seventh chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 7 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the small kindnesses (al-ma'un) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as the characteristics of those who deny the Day of Judgment, the neglect of orphans and the needy, the insincerity in prayer, and the withholding of small acts of kindness and charity.

1.name: Al-Kawthar
1.overview: It is the one hundred and eighth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 3 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the abundance (al-kawthar) mentioned in it, referring to the river granted to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Paradise. It addresses themes such as the abundant blessings bestowed upon the Prophet ﷺ, the command to pray and sacrifice in gratitude, and the reassurance that his detractors will be cut off.

1.name: Al-Kafirun
1.overview: It is the one hundred and ninth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 6 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the disbelievers (al-kafirun) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the clear declaration of disavowal from polytheism, the distinction between the worship of the believers and the worship of the disbelievers, and the freedom of each to follow their own religion.

1.name: An-Nasr
1.overview: It is the one hundred and tenth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 3 verses. It is a Medinan surah that takes its name from the victory (an-nasr) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as the victory granted by God, the coming of people in crowds to embrace Islam, and the command to glorify and praise God and seek His forgiveness.

1.name: Al-Masad
1.overview: It is the one hundred and eleventh chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 5 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the palm fiber (al-masad) mentioned in it. It addresses the fate of Abu Lahab and his wife, who were among the fiercest opponents of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, declaring their wealth and actions will be of no benefit to them and that they will face the punishment of the Fire.

1.name: Al-Ikhlas
1.overview: It is the one hundred and twelfth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 4 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from sincerity (al-ikhlas) mentioned in it. It addresses the pure Oneness of God, affirming that He is One, Eternal and Absolute, neither begotten nor begetting, and that there is none comparable to Him.

1.name: Al-Falaq
1.overview: It is the one hundred and thirteenth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 5 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from the daybreak (al-falaq) mentioned at its beginning. It addresses themes such as seeking refuge in God from the evil of creation, the darkness of night, sorcery and envy, and the protection of God from all harms.

1.name: An-Nas
1.overview: It is the one hundred and fourteenth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 6 verses. It is a Makkan surah that takes its name from mankind (an-nas) mentioned in it. It addresses themes such as seeking refuge in God, the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, and the God of mankind, from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws—the devil who whispers into the hearts of people, from among the jinn and mankind.

lastEpisodeToAir.name: Aal Imran
lastEpisodeToAir.overview: Surah Aal-Imran teaches that true faith requires conviction, obedience, unity, patience, and steadfastness. Through the stories of earlier prophets and the lessons of Uhud, it encourages believers to remain faithful to Allah and His guidance even when facing trials.

nextEpisodeToAir.name: An-Nisa
nextEpisodeToAir.overview: It is the fourth chapter (surah) of the Holy Quran, consisting of 176 verses. It is a Medinan surah that addresses many issues related to women, family, inheritance, and marriage. It also discusses the rights of orphans, the People of the Book, and matters of justice and community life.

seasons.name: Season 1
seasons.overview: The Holy Quran (also spelled Qur'an or Koran) is the sacred scripture of Islam. Muslims believe it is the word of Allah (God), revealed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through the Angel Gabriel (Jibril) over approximately 23 years, beginning around 610 CE.  ترجم
